title: Conditional sentences (1)
summary: Четыре типа условных предложений (zero, first, second, third), выбор между реальным и нереальным условием, were вместо was, смешанные условные и модальные глаголы в главной части.
ru:
## Реальное или нереальное: как выбрать тип
Вы знаете четыре типа условных предложений. На уровне Advanced главное — понимать, **как говорящий оценивает ситуацию**, а не просто механически подставлять формы.
- **Zero conditional**: if + present simple, present simple — общие истины и закономерности (if = «всякий раз, когда»). *If you heat ice, it melts.*
- **First conditional**: if + present, will — реальное, вполне возможное будущее. *If prices rise again, we'll have to cut costs.*
- **Second conditional**: if + past simple, would — нереальное или маловероятное настоящее / будущее. *If I won the lottery, I'd quit my job.*
- **Third conditional**: if + past perfect, would have + V3 — нереальное прошлое. *If I had known, I would have helped.*

## Одна ситуация — две оценки
Разница между first и second — в вероятности, а не во времени:
> If you **come** tomorrow, I'll show you the lab. — Приходи, вполне возможно; я покажу.
> If you **came** tomorrow, I'd show you the lab. — Гипотетически (скорее всего, ты не придёшь / это маловероятно).
Поэтому, когда речь о реальном плане, second conditional звучит холодно или вежливо-дистанцированно: *If you could send the file today, I'd be grateful.*

## If I were … и if I was
В формальной речи и в советах используется **were** для всех лиц: *If I **were** you, I'd accept the offer.* В разговоре **was** с I / he / she / it допустимо, но в устойчивой фразе **If I were you** лучше сохранять were. Конструкция **were to + инфинитив** делает событие ещё менее вероятным: *If I were to win, I'd donate the prize.*
- ~~If I would be you~~ → **If I were you**

## Смешанные условные
Время условия и время результата могут не совпадать:
- **прошлое условие → настоящий результат**: if + past perfect, would + V: *If I **had taken** the job in Dubai, I'd **be living** there now.* — Если бы я тогда согласился на работу в Дубае, жил бы там сейчас.
- **постоянное свойство → прошлый результат**: if + past simple, would have + V3: *If she **were** less stubborn, she **would have accepted** help.* — Будь она менее упряма, приняла бы помощь.
~~If I would have known~~ — частая ошибка: **would не ставим** в if-части: If I **had known**.

## Что может стоять в разных частях
- В главной части вместо will / would: **might, could, may, should, must**, повелительное наклонение. *If you see Tom, tell him to call me. / If it's sunny, we might go sailing.*
- В if-части возможны **present perfect** (завершённость): *If you've finished the report, send it to me.* и **continuous**: *If you're going to the shop, get some milk.*
- ~~If it will rain tomorrow, we'll stay in.~~ → If it **rains** tomorrow, we'll stay in.

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~If I will see her, I'll tell her.~~ → If I **see** her, I'll tell her.
- ~~If I would know the answer, I'd tell you.~~ → If I **knew** the answer, I'd tell you.
- ~~If you would have asked, I would have helped.~~ → If you **had asked**, I would have helped.
en:
## Real or unreal: choosing the type
You know the four types of conditional sentences. At Advanced level the key is **how the speaker sees the situation**, not just the forms.
- **Zero conditional**: if + present simple, present simple. General truths (if = whenever). *If you heat ice, it melts.*
- **First conditional**: if + present, will. A real, likely future. *If prices rise again, we'll have to cut costs.*
- **Second conditional**: if + past simple, would. Unreal or unlikely present or future. *If I won the lottery, I'd quit my job.*
- **Third conditional**: if + past perfect, would have + past participle. Unreal past. *If I had known, I would have helped.*

## One situation, two attitudes
The difference between first and second is probability, not time:
> If you **come** tomorrow, I'll show you the lab. (it is quite possible)
> If you **came** tomorrow, I'd show you the lab. (it is unlikely / hypothetical)
Second conditional can also sound polite and distant: *If you could send the file today, I'd be grateful.*

## If I were ... and if I was
In formal English and in advice we use **were** with all persons: *If I **were** you, I'd accept the offer.* In casual speech **was** is possible with I / he / she / it, but keep **were** in **If I were you**. **were to + infinitive** makes the event even less likely: *If I were to win, I'd donate the prize.*
- ~~If I would be you~~ → **If I were you**

## Mixed conditionals
The time of the condition and the time of the result may differ:
- **past condition → present result**: if + past perfect, would + verb: *If I **had taken** the job in Dubai, I'd **be living** there now.*
- **permanent quality → past result**: if + past simple, would have + past participle: *If she **were** less stubborn, she **would have accepted** help.*
~~If I would have known~~ is a common mistake: do **not** use would in the if-part: If I **had known**.

## What can appear in each part
- In the main clause instead of will / would: **might, could, may, should, must**, or an imperative. *If you see Tom, tell him to call me. / If it's sunny, we might go sailing.*
- In the if-clause: the **present perfect** (completion) *If you've finished the report, send it to me.* or a **continuous** form: *If you're going to the shop, get some milk.*
- ~~If it will rain tomorrow~~ → If it **rains** tomorrow

## Common mistakes
- ~~If I will see her~~ → If I **see** her
- ~~If I would know the answer~~ → If I **knew** the answer
- ~~If you would have asked~~ → If you **had asked**
structure:
## Четыре типа
| Тип | if-часть | Главная часть | Значение | Пример |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| zero | present simple | present simple | закономерность | If you heat ice, it melts. |
| first | present simple / perfect | will / can / imperative | реальное будущее | If it rains, we'll stay in. |
| second | past simple (were) | would / could / might + V | нереальное сейчас | If I had time, I'd learn Greek. |
| third | past perfect | would have + V3 | нереальное прошлое | If I'd known, I'd have called. |
| mixed (1) | past perfect | would + V | прошлое → сейчас | If I'd gone, I'd be rich now. |
| mixed (2) | past simple | would have + V3 | сейчас → прошлое | If she were kinder, she'd have helped. |

## Формулы
> **If** + past perfect, **would** + V (результат сейчас)
> **If** + past simple, **would have** + V3 (результат в прошлом)
> **If I were you**, I would + V (совет)
> **If** + subject + **were to** + V, ... (маловероятное событие)

## Запомните
- В if-части **не** ставим will / would (кроме вежливых просьб, см. следующий юнит).
- Сокращения: had → 'd, would → 'd: If I'd known, I'd have called.

exercises.title: Формы глаголов
exercises.instruction: Поставьте глагол в скобках в нужную форму (если возможны варианты — достаточно одного).
exercises.example: If I (know) about the delay, I would have taken a train. → **had known**

items.text: If {{I had known|I'd known}} about the delay, I would have taken the train.
If prices {{rise|go up|increase}} again next month, we'll have to cut costs.
If she {{were|was}} my colleague, I'd ask her to lead the project.
Water {{boils}} if you heat it to 100 degrees at sea level.
If {{I had taken|I'd taken}} the job in Dubai, I'd be living there now.
{{We would have won|We'd have won}} the match if the goalkeeper hadn't been injured.
If {{you have finished|you've finished}} the report, please send it to me.
If it {{weren't|were not|wasn't|was not}} so expensive, I'd buy it.
If I {{were|was}} you, I'd accept the offer.
If the train {{is|gets}} delayed, we'll miss the connection.
If I hadn't missed the flight, I {{would be|'d be}} in Rome now.
If {{you had told|you'd told}} me earlier, I could have helped.
If I {{won|were to win|was to win}} the lottery, I'd quit my job.
If you {{don't water|do not water}} the plants, they die.
If we hadn't taken a taxi, we {{would have missed|might have missed|could have missed}} the start.
If it {{rains|should rain}} tomorrow, the match will be moved indoors.

exercises.instruction: Выберите форму, подходящую по смыслу и грамматике.

items.q: If you ___ the fuse, the lights come back on.
items.why: Закономерность (zero conditional) — present simple в обеих частях.

items.q: If I ___ more time, I would learn Japanese.
If I ___ the lottery, I would travel round the world.
items.why: Маловероятное будущее — past simple, would в if-части не ставим.

items.q: If she ___ harder, she would have passed.
I'd have called you if I ___ your number.
items.why: Третий тип: if + past perfect (had had = past perfect от have).

items.q: If he ___ the sales manager, he would know the figures.
items.why: Нереальное настоящее: **were** (допустимо и was, но в тесте — were).

items.q: If I ___ to the meeting yesterday, I'd know what was agreed.
items.why: Смешанный тип: прошлое условие (past perfect), результат сейчас (would know).

items.q: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ the match.
items.why: Реальное будущее — первый тип, в главной части will.

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Ответьте полными предложениями, выбирая нужный тип условного.

items.prompt: What will you do if the weather is good this weekend? (first conditional)
items.sample: If the weather is good this weekend, I'll go cycling in the park.

items.prompt: What would you do if you could live anywhere in the world? (second conditional)
items.sample: If I could live anywhere, I'd choose a small town by the sea.

items.prompt: Name a past decision and what might have happened otherwise. (third conditional)
items.sample: If I hadn't studied English, I wouldn't have got this job.

items.prompt: Describe how a past event affects your life now. (mixed conditional)
items.sample: If I hadn't moved to a new city, I wouldn't be working in IT now.
